task.description: Produce the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req187-timer-engine-wiring.md or similar) for REQ-187's full scope: (1) transition/3's handling of a token arriving at a :TIMER node -- compute fire_at = arrival timestamp + parsed duration_iso8601, and RETURN a description of the timer to be armed using the SAME existing return-shape pattern transition.ex already uses for other impure effects (name exactly which shape is extended and how) -- transition.ex itself must gain NO Repo call; (2) the impure caller (identify which module actually calls transition/3 and persists its return value -- likely lib/letflow/engine.ex) must, upon seeing a timer-arm effect, call REQ-186's Scheduler.create/2 with a caller-supplied Multi so the timer row and the state-transition event commit in ONE transaction; (3) firing behavior -- when REQ-186's poller fires a timer, the instance must advance along the TIMER node's outgoing edge (specify exactly how the poller's fire path triggers this -- does it call back into the engine's own transition/completion machinery, or does Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 need a callback/hook point?); (4) cancellation -- replace cancel_pending_timers/2's no-op with a real update setting every PENDING timer for that instance to cancelled (with cancelled_at + cancel_reason) on the caller-supplied repo/prefix, preserving the exact call site in engine.ex L1177 (do not relocate it), plus add the equivalent call inside cancel_instance/3's own transaction per the L234-242 deferral (timer half only -- REQ-056's SERVICE_TASK HTTP-abort half stays deferred, do not touch it); (5) the SCH-03 concurrency edge case -- state precisely how a fired timer is never touched by a later cancellation (a status-guarded UPDATE, e.g. only affecting rows still 'pending'), and how a race between the poller mid-fire and a concurrent cancellation resolves via normal transaction commit-ordering (first commit wins, other rolls back) without any additional locking beyond what already exists. Design only -- no fenced code blocks reproducing real .ex content (this project's mechanical no-exceptions rule, hit repeatedly in this pipeline -- be deliberate about avoiding it).
acceptance_criteria: a definition containing a TIMER node with a valid duration_iso8601 starts an instance whose token reaches that node and arms exactly one timers row with status 'pending' and fire_at equal to the arrival timestamp plus the parsed duration -- replacing the {:error, {:node_type_not_yet_implemented, :TIMER, _}} that transition.ex L294 returns today, asserted by a test that would have failed before this requirement
the timer row and the state-transition event are written in ONE transaction: a test that forces the event append to fail leaves NO timers row behind
when the timer fires, the instance advances along the TIMER node's outgoing edge and the token is no longer at the TIMER node

completing an instance sets every one of its PENDING timers to 'cancelled' with cancelled_at set, via the existing TaskActivation.cancel_pending_timers/2 call site in engine.ex -- which is still called from the same position inside the completion transaction (confirmed by git diff showing the call site itself unmoved)

cancelling an instance via Letflow.Engine.cancel_instance/3 likewise cancels its PENDING timers in the same transaction, and a test forcing that transaction to roll back leaves the timers still 'pending'

a timer whose status is already 'fired' is NOT changed by a subsequent instance cancellation (SCH-03's stated edge case), and no PENDING timer belonging to a CANCELLED or COMPLETED instance is ever fired by a later poll -- two explicit tests

lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex contains no Letflow.Repo call after this change, confirmed by the same grep its moduledoc already documents for purity, and the moduledoc names which return shape was extended to carry the timer-arming description instead
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
